Senses.PreferredTarget: Complete Command of the Precious Mirror
AlternateTargets: Song of the Complete Command of the Precious Mirror
Senses.Note: #0g deviation: the phrase is deployed as the proper name of a Caodong transmission text and house inheritance, not merely as the ordinary image of a valuable mirror or the standalone word for complete command. Attribution of authorship is not fully uniform: Dongshan's record says he received it from Yunyan and entrusted it to Caoshan; later records also call it Dongshan's text or report older attributions. The entry therefore reports the transmission claims without deciding authorship. Allowlisted count: 117 hits in 49 texts; the title form “Song of the Complete Command of the Precious Mirror” one text.

SearchAliases: Complete Command of the Precious Mirror
Senses.Explanation: In the records this is a transmitted Caodong verse and named textual object, described as a complete command and passed from teacher to successor. In the Chan record this is not a generic state: it is the title and transmitted Caodong text associated with Dongshan Liangjie. Dongshan tells Caoshan that he personally received the Complete Command of the Precious Mirror from his former teacher Yunyan, that its matter exhausts the essential point, and that he now entrusts it to Caoshan (吾在雲巖先師處親印寶鏡三昧，事窮的要，今付于汝). A later commentary consequently calls it a book transmitted privately by Dongshan to Caoshan (寶鏡三昧一書，洞山室中密授曹山者也). The text itself opens, “This such thing was secretly entrusted by buddhas and ancestors; you have now obtained it, so guard it well” (如是之法，佛祖密付；汝今得之，宜善保護), then gives the paired images “a silver bowl filled with snow; the bright moon hiding a heron” (銀盌盛雪，明月藏鷺) and says that although their kinds are not the same, mixed together their places are known (類之弗齊，混則知處). Across later Caodong records its title is joined to the Five Ranks, upright and crooked, ruler and minister, and the paired wording “he is not me; I am precisely he” (‘he is not me; I am precisely he’). A direct question, “What is the Complete Command of the Precious Mirror?” receives, “Do not reflect idle light and shadows; return his old face” (不照閒光影，還他舊面皮). These are the transmitted title, contents, relations, and recorded answer; the corpus supplies no single prose substitution for the whole text.

Senses.Explanation: The (延壽堂), literally 'hall for extending life,' is the monastery infirmary where sick monastics are housed and tended. Rulebooks list its supervisor among the communal offices and describe appointing a conscientious person; Mingjue Cong recounts spending three months there with a grave illness, while Langting Jingting raises the case of an unnamed monk who dies in the hall. The auspicious name does not turn it into a longevity shrine.
